brief: GS Credit MarketStrats argues technicals are aligning for a near-term relief rally, independent of whether Middle East risk or rate-hike scope is fundamentally resolved. USD and EUR rates have sold off over 80bps YTD to near 15-year wides, with the market pricing 3+ Fed and ECB hikes over 12 months. CTA rates positioning is the shortest since April 2026 ($171mm DV01 short, concentrated in JGBs/Bobl/Bunds), equity Sentiment Indicator reads -0.92, and AAII bull-bear is very negative, together raising short-squeeze risk. This positioning skew argues for a relief rally even if not fundamentally justified, giving credit spreads room to squeeze over 1-2 months; the author recommends underweight credit investors add tactical upside via short-dated iTraxx Main receivers (funded by selling payers) and longer-duration EUR IG Senior Financials cash (GSLCIF5Y, ~96bps to benchmark, 4.36% yield). Separately: hyperscaler credit has outperformed and the author is starting to monetize/trim those longs on further rallies; the long EUR IG cash vs short iTraxx Main basis trade remains a high-conviction RV call; short Xover 5y vs long Main 10y decomp stays the preferred bearish hedge against higher-rate downside; and French OAT-Bund and IG spreads continue widening on election-cycle fiscal risk, with elevated bank primary issuance prefunding into 2027.
